answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a umber as the anchor of the cost.
